content.text: Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling 2025 is the State Counselling procedure for admission to Ayush Courses: BAMS/BNYS/BUMS/BSMS/BHMS, supervised by the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy, Chennai. The NEET examination qualification conducted by the NTA is the preliminary criterion for admission to these courses in Tamil Nadu. TN Ayush Counselling is conducted for seats in private and government colleges in the state, which are approved by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the National Commission for Homeopathy (NCH) under both state and All India Quota.
The NEET-UG 2025 exam was held on 4 May 2025, and the results were out on 14 June 2025. The starting dates of TN Ayush Counselling are yet to be released.
This article will provide you with the complete information regarding the counselling procedure, including important dates, fees, and cutoff.

sections.heading: Ayush Counselling in Tamil Nadu Overview

content.text: Ayush Counselling in Tamil Nadu is conducted by the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy, Chennai , for admission to Ayurveda, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha & Homeopathy courses in private and government colleges of Tamil Nadu. http://www.tnhealth.tn.gov.in is the official website for TN Ayush Counselling, where the candidates shall register themselves to apply to the Ayush colleges. The candidates who qualified the NEET-UG examination of the present academic year and have 10+2 with science stream and subjects, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, are eligible to participate in the counselling.

The state counselling mainly reserves 85% of the seats for the domicile students of Tamil Nadu under the State Quota. The remaining 15% of seats are open to all candidates, including students from other states under the All India Quota (AIQ). The counselling for the AIQ seats to private and government colleges in Tamil Nadu is handled by the AACCC .
There are a total of 18 BAMS colleges , 18 BNYS colleges, 1 Unani college (BUMS), 15 Siddha colleges (BSMS), and 14 BHMS, Homeopathy colleges in Tamil Nadu, participating in the counselling.

sections.heading: Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling Process- State Quota

content.text: Here’s the detailed procedure for Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling for applying to the state quota.

items: The NEET qualified candidates must register themselves with the official website of the state counselling authority at www.tnhealth.tn.gov.in and fill out the application form with necessary personal and academic details.
Download the application form and, along with the relevant document, send it to the concerned authority.
Make payment of the application fee according to the respective category of the candidates to confirm registration.
Attend the document verification process at the designated centers with the original certificates. They can be retrieved after the verification.
Log in to the official website with your credentials and fill in the choices of colleges in the option entry form.
Arrange the list of colleges according to your preference.
It is mandatory to lock the choices before the last date.
Seat allotment is made in multiple rounds, including a mop-up round and a stray vacancy round.
The Stray Vacancy round is conducted only for the vacant seats that remain after the previous rounds of allotment.
The results of the allotment are published on the official website. Log in with your credentials to access the list.
Allotment of seats is made on the basis of the NEET scores, Merit rank, Reservation policy, and the Choices of Colleges.
Download the allotment letter if you are allotted to a college.
After the allotment results are published, the candidates should join the allotted college within the time frame specified.
Carry the original documents and certificates along with the Allotment letter to the college for verification.
Complete the admission formalities and confirm seat at the college by making payment of the college fees.

sections.heading: Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling Process- All India Quota

content.text: The All India Quota seats counselling is conducted by the Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC) . The candidates should register themselves with the official website of AACCC at aaccc.gov.in for the counselling.

The candidates can directly apply through the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homeopathy (DIMH), Tamil Nadu, for self-financing colleges by downloading the application form from the website of www.tnhealth.tn.gov.in.
Here is the detailed procedure for applying under the India Quota (AIQ) for Tamil Nadu Ayush Counselling.

items: Visit the official website of AACCC at https://aaccc.gov.in/ and click on the registration link.
Fill out the application form with personal details. Incorrect information may affect the eligibility of the candidate.
Make payment of the registration fees as prescribed for the respective category.
Upload scanned original documents and certificates to complete the registration.
Choice filling round enables the candidates to fill out the options entry form with the list of preferred colleges and the state.
Candidates can select Tamil Nadu state and arrange the colleges in the list according to their preference.
It is mandatory to lock the choices within the specified deadline.
The allotment process involves multiple rounds: Round 1/Round 2/Mop-up Round/Stray Vacancy Round.
The rules and participation for every round are different.
Seats are allotted on the basis of merit rank, NEET scores, reservation policy, and choices of colleges.
Provisional and final lists of Allotment are published on the official website of AACCC.
Log in to the portal with your credentials and download the allotment letter if you are allotted a college.
The candidates who are allotted colleges must report to the respective college within the time frame provided.
Carry the relevant original documents and certificates for verification at the college.
Complete the admission procedure with payment of the college fees within the prescribed time.

The private and government colleges recognized by the NCISM, NCH, and the Ministry of Ayush participate in the counselling. Domicile students can apply under the 85% seats of the State Quota, and students from other states can apply for 15% of the seats under the AIQ through AACCC. It is mandatory for candidates to have higher secondary education with the minimum prescribed percentage in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, along with the NEET-UG qualification, to be eligible for TN Ayush Counselling.
